Apple has been waiting a very long time to launch its first foldable iPhone, while Samsung's Galaxy Z Fold series has already reached its eighth generation.

Apple had every reason to hold back from the start, but based on Samsung's latest experience, the timing for the iPhone maker to make its move could hardly be more perfect…

Apple's Long Wait

Samsung was one of the earliest companies to embrace foldable smartphones enthusiastically, but quickly discovered it had rushed in too soon. The first-generation Samsung Galaxy Fold had an extremely fragile display prone to damage, and the company ultimately had to pull it from sale.

Meanwhile, Apple waited patiently for the display technology to mature — needing not only significantly greater durability, but also the absence of a visible crease when unfolded. Reports indicate Apple even had to send its own design engineers to help Samsung achieve this.

Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Proves the Timing Is Right

We mentioned last month that the display used in Samsung's Galaxy Z Fold 8 is extremely similar to that of the upcoming iPhone Ultra. Our sister site 9to5Google found that the new device truly delivers on its promise — once unfolded, the crease in the middle of the display is virtually invisible.

However, the significance goes beyond Samsung finally solving the display technology issue; consumer demand has also finally arrived. 9to5Google reported that initial demand for the Fold 8 is three times that of its predecessor.

This figure builds on the 50% growth in demand seen last year.

Of course, these two things are likely interrelated — a creaseless display dramatically boosts appeal — but factoring in last year's growth rate, it's clear that foldable phones have been around for some time now, and more people are beginning to see the benefits of this form factor.

The iPhone Ultra is expected to debut next month alongside the iPhone 18 Pro lineup. The new device is anticipated to quickly capture approximately 25% of the overall foldable smartphone market.
